:::{#exm-circle}
#### Points on a circle

Take the [circle](#def-circle) with center $\va = (1, 2)$ and radius $r = 5$.
The point $\vx = (4, 6)$ is on it:

$$
\ba
\norm{\vx - \va}
&= \sqrt{(4 - 1)^2 + (6 - 2)^2}
&& \text{(@def-euclidean-distance)}
\\
&= \sqrt{9 + 16}
&& \text{(subtract and square)}
\\
&= 5.
&& \text{(add and take the square root)}
\ea
$$

The center $(1, 2)$ itself is not on the circle,
because its distance from $\va$ is $0$, not $5$.

:::{#fig-circle-example}

```{r}
#| label: circle-example-plot
#| code-fold: true
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   A circle of radius 5 around the point (1, 2), drawn on equal axes. A
#|   hollow dot marks the center (1, 2), a solid dot marks the point (4, 6)
#|   on the circle, and a dashed segment of length 5 joins them.
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-width: 4.5
# The circle with center (1, 2) and radius 5, traced by its angle.
angle <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 400)
circle <- tibble::tibble(
  x1 = 1 + 5 * cos(angle),
  x2 = 2 + 5 * sin(angle)
)
marks <- tibble::tribble(
  ~x1, ~x2, ~label, ~kind,
  1, 2, "center (1, 2)", "center",
  4, 6, "(4, 6)", "on the circle"
)
radius <- tibble::tibble(x1 = 1, x2 = 2, x1_end = 4, x2_end = 6)
shapes <- c(center = 1, "on the circle" = 16)

circle |>
  ggplot2::ggplot() +
  ggplot2::aes(x = x1, y = x2) +
  ggplot2::geom_path() +
  ggplot2::geom_segment(
    data = radius,
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(xend = x1_end, yend = x2_end),
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    data = marks,
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(shape = kind),
    size = 3
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_text(
    data = marks,
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(label = label),
    vjust = -1
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_shape_manual(values = shapes, guide = "none") +
  ggplot2::coord_fixed() +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "first coordinate", y = "second coordinate")
```

The [circle](#def-circle) with center $(1, 2)$ and radius $5$.
The dashed segment from the center to $(4, 6)$ is $5$ units long.
:::
